text:
maya: Heads up — onboarding Elysium-8B (converted from Gemma format) on dedicated. Did an int4 quant run and our summarization eval dropped noticeably on redwood-evals.
maya: Quick results: fp16 baseline Rouge-L 38.1 -> int4 34.7, perplexity dev fp16 12.3 -> int4 15.8. Not huge but reproducible across seeds.
maya: I think it's not pure quant noise — found some token id remapping in the conversion that looks like it shifts a few diacritic/ZWJ-heavy tokens.
maya: snippet of tokenizer inspect + first tokens after conversion:
```python
>>> toks = tok.encode("Th66e — café")
>>> toks
[54, 1023, 4096, 0, 771]
# on converted model these map to [54, 1024, 4096, 0, 772] occasionally
```
maya: Also saw small rotary misalignment when running long-context (hot-reload test). Samples show drift in factual recall after ~1.2k tokens.
sam: hmm. two suspects: (1) vocab id shift during the Gemma->Elysium conversion, (2) rotary frequency/base mismatch (freq_scale or headwise factors).
sam: can you run `scripts/check_vocab_map.py --dump-mapping <converted> <orig>` and paste the first 200 entries? that usually shows off-by-one slips.
liam: also check kv-cache warmup: if head ordering or per-head rotary params differ, the kvcache indexing will misalign and cause longctx degradation. I hit similar with Orion-RT onboarding.
liam: quick grep I run:
```bash
# check rotary params
python -c "import torch,sys; m=torch.load(sys.argv[1], map_location='cpu'); print(m['rotary_scale'][:8])" converted.pt
```
eva: eval-bot: redwood-evals summary (run 2026-03-22T14:12Z)
```text
suite: summarization-small
models: fp16_baseline, int4_converted
fp16_baseline: Rouge-L 38.1, BLEU 21.4
int4_converted: Rouge-L 34.7, BLEU 18.9
notes: failure modes cluster around sentences with accented chars and multiple zero-width joiners
```
eva: also ran token-level hit-rate check: 0.3% token id mismatch on conversion (mostly in unicode combining ranges)
maya: thanks. I ran the mapping dump — ~220 mismatches in the 0..50k range, concentrated on 0x0300-0x036F zone. attaching sample in thread (abridged).
maya: hypothesis: conversion script used NFC normalization and the original vocab used NFKC or had explicit ZWJ entries -> some tokens shifted by +1. That explains small but systematic perf delta.
sam: if true, two mitigations: (A) remap token ids in the embedding matrix to preserve original semantics (cheap), (B) rebuild tokenizer to exact original normalizer and rerun quantization (safer long-term).
sam: for (A) we have script `scripts/embed_remap.sh` — but need to ensure headwise rotary params stay paired with head indices after remap.
liam: want me to try remap+int4-reserialize on a snapshot? I can run on a dev dedicated GPU tonight. if we get Rouge-L back to baseline, we know it's vocab-only.
maya: please do. I'll also try re-quant with `--preserve-vocab-order` flag and toggle `rotary_scale` between 1.0 and 1.25 to see sensitivity.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: snapshot elysium-conv-int4-20260322 queued for dev cluster (req id: rq_8f3b). ETA ~45m.
maya: thx infra-bot. tagging @sam @liam — will post results here. :coffee:
